stage_a.note: Very enthusiastic, smiling, confident delivery of a humorous product.
High energy, expressive gestures, passionate about solving the problem.
Friendly, approachable, uses humor to connect with the panel.

venture.description: A specialized towel designed to absorb under-breast sweat for women.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin introduces herself, her company, and her ask, then describes the problem of under-breast sweat and her towel solution.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if women wear the towel outside.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin clarifies that she originally designed it for use when getting out of the shower.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if the towel is tightened from the neck.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms that it is.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if it also tightens underneath.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms and explains that it keeps everything in place even when moving around.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what size breasts the product is designed for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin states the size range goes from a large C cup up to an H cup.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin hands out samples of the product to the panel.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori jokes about trying the towel on Kevin's head.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin hands Kevin a towel with grapefruits inside to simulate the weight.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he does not need the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara points out that the towels make great gifts.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin puts the towel around his neck and says it could work.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin compliments Kevin on how the towel looks on him.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark puts a towel on his head and laughs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if Erin has secured a patent for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms she has a patent and trademark registered in the US and China.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks whether it is a design or utility patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin clarifies it is a design patent, with a second patent pending for a maternity version.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks for the retail price of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin provides the retail prices for both the original and maternity versions.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks for the manufacturing cost per unit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin states the cost to make each towel.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks for the total number of units sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin reveals she has sold over a million dollars worth in twelve months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin expresses surprise at the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori is also amazed by the sales volume.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara congratulates Erin on her margins and sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin thanks Barbara for the compliment.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if all sales are conducted online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms she sells exclusively through her own website.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark assumes Erin is making a lot of money and doing very well.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin shares her background story, explaining how she quit her job and started making the towels herself.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert compliments Erin on her achievements.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin describes how her product unexpectedly went viral online, leading to a massive surge in sales.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies that the viral success happened organically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms the viral moment happened on its own.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks if the product is still manufactured domestically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin proudly confirms that her products are handmade by women in an eco-friendly facility in Los Angeles.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if she could raise the price given the domestic, handmade manufacturing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark points out that her current profit margins are relatively low.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin explains that copycats disrupted her business after she went viral, forcing her to pause operations.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if Erin took action to enforce her patent against the copycats.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms that they did enforce the patent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks for her projected sales for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin projects two million dollars in sales for the year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for her actual sales figures year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin states her sales for the first six months.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert clarifies if that figure is for the whole year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark questions the feasibility of jumping from her current sales to the two million dollar projection.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin insists it is possible due to global demand and her previous need to halt operations.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks for her specific plan to achieve that massive growth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin begins to answer but is interrupted.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert reiterates the concern about the massive required jump in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin argues that the product's effectiveness will drive the necessary sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara challenges this, noting that a good product alone does not guarantee the required sales volume in six months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin counters by stating she has the necessary inventory ready to sell.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for the exact amount of inventory she currently holds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin states the number of units she has in stock.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin mistakenly calculates the retail value of her inventory as two million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin corrects him, providing the actual retail value of her current inventory.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark breaks down the math, arguing her inventory turnover rate makes her projection impossible without another viral event.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin suggests QVC as a potential channel to move the inventory.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if Erin has actually initiated conversations with QVC.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin admits she has not yet spoken to QVC.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark insists her sales projection is unrealistic without another unpredictable viral moment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin admits she needs help moving her inventory but points to consistent global sales as a positive sign.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark decides to exit, citing her unrealistic projections and scattered approach to global expansion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin thanks Mark for his time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin points out that admitting she does not know how to sell her inventory is a red flag.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin concedes she should not have phrased her need for help that way.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin notes her statement reveals a lack of a concrete strategic plan.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert points out that the product is currently not selling fast enough.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin argues that her current inventory would sell out instantly if she went viral again.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert challenges her reliance on going viral, noting it cannot be predicted or scheduled.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin agrees but notes she is now prepared with inventory if it happens again.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert criticizes her for relying on a past, unrepeatable event to solve her current sales problem.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin defends her position by highlighting how far she has already come.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert decides to exit, stating that hope is not a viable business strategy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin thanks Robert.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin decides to exit, stating he needs a partner with a clear plan to reach the projected sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin thanks Kevin.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges the current valuation of the company, suggesting it is worth less than the ask.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin defends the valuation by pointing to the value of her existing inventory.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates his decision to exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin acknowledges his decision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara decides to exit, expressing concern over the declining sales trajectory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin acknowledges Barbara's decision.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert notes that Lori is the only investor remaining.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori offers the requested capital but demands half the company, citing the significant work required.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin laughs at the steep equity demand.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori restates her offer, promising to make Erin a millionaire through their partnership.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin counters Lori's offer, asking if she would accept a much lower equity stake.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori flatly rejects the counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin slightly increases her counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori defends her high equity ask by reminding Erin of her declining sales and need for significant help.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks Erin if there are any conditions under which she would give up half her company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin refuses, explaining she already gave up some equity to an early investor and wants to retain control.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori revises her offer, reducing her equity demand while keeping the capital the same.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin counters again, asking for a slightly lower equity stake.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark uses a fruit analogy to encourage Erin to take the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin appreciates the joke and notes she has watermelons on set.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin urges Erin to make a final decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin asks Lori if she would increase the investment amount for the requested equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara tells the other investors to let Erin think and speak.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin confirms the terms of Lori's revised final offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori assures Erin that their partnership will be highly successful.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin tells Erin that a small difference in equity will not matter in the long run.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara reminds Erin that she must be comfortable with whatever deal she makes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin acknowledges her mistakes and expresses gratitude for the offer and the needed help.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin presses Erin for her final answer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin accepts Lori's revised offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori cheers the accepted deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin thanks Lori profusely.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori approaches Erin for a celebratory hug.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks about the fruit used in the demonstration.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about the size and comfort of the fruit in his towel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin mentions she is trying not to cry from happiness.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori reassures Erin that it is okay to show emotion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Erin calls for a group hug with her models.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he is also going to cry.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark congratulates Erin on securing a deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin also offers his congratulations.

exchanges.label: price, cost, and viral sales history

decisions.note: Unrealistic projections and scattered approach to global expansion.
Strategy is based on hope rather than a concrete plan.
Needs a partner who can show exactly how to reach the projected sales.
Concerned that sales are sliding versus going up.
Wants a larger stake due to the significant work required.
Reluctant to give up half the company.
Reduces her equity demand as her best offer.
Attempts to negotiate the equity down further.
